claims.claim: Repository policy defaults are exactly Codex gpt-6-sol/medium and Antigravity gemini-3.8-flash/medium, and tests prove the policy remains the sole default authority with no adapter, carrier, workflow, CLI, or test duplicate default constants.

Local run and continue, including continue delegation into PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and coding REPAIR, accept partial or complete Human model and effort overrides for Codex and Antigravity, and the direct canonical REMEDIATION and coding REPAIR surfaces preserve the same semantics. Omitted dimensions resolve deterministically, EXPLICIT versus REPOSITORY_DEFAULT attribution is preserved, and the exact resolved values reach native command construction.

A new authorization never implicitly inherits the previous RUN profile, while replay, restart, or reconciliation of the same authorization reuses its exact already-bound profile even after repository defaults change, and never re-resolves changed defaults.

PRIMARY remote carrier v3 validates one exact Human request, resolves one exact profile from the canonical policy, propagates it through self-host delivery, and binds it into a new profile-aware durable PRIMARY dispatch identity before RUN native execution, without later re-resolution or silent substitution.

REMEDIATION intent v2 and REPAIR wakeup v2 carriers and durable journal records provide the same exact request-resolution, workflow propagation, durable dispatch binding, idempotent replay, and changed-profile collision rejection guarantees as PRIMARY, including rejection of newly submitted legacy carrier request versions.

New profile-aware dispatch records and the eventual per-RUN TASK-162 execution-profile sidecar agree exactly on executor, model, reasoning_effort, model_source, and effort_source attribution. Any disagreement, invalid effort, malformed profile selection, or conflicting persisted sidecar fails before any native Executor invocation.

Historical PRIMARY v1 and v2, REMEDIATION v1, and REPAIR v1 durable journals remain readable and reconcilable under their exact historical semantics. Replaying or reconciling such an existing identity does not resolve, attach, compare against, or persist current repository defaults, does not upgrade the journal version, and does not fabricate execution-profile provenance or a new native authorization. Newly submitted legacy carrier request versions are rejected rather than silently applying current defaults.

Invalid effort, malformed model identifier, missing required Executor or profile context, and profile options supplied to the Antigravity MiniMax adapter invoke zero native Executors. Existing Antigravity MiniMax execution without model or effort override options remains behaviorally unchanged, and overrides are never silently applied to MiniMax.

A syntactically valid explicit alternate or future provider-native model identifier can flow end-to-end through local and remote profile binding without source-code registration or a repository-global allowlist. Native provider rejection of an exact syntactically valid model remains an ordinary no-fallback native execution failure.

Remote operational receipts may retain bounded exact profile selectors where relevant for diagnosis, but they remain subordinate operational observations and never claim RUN creation, native success, Runtime verification, semantic review, or publication beyond directly proven boundaries, and existing carrier receipts still avoid asserting such success from workflow completion alone.

Frozen TASK, RUN, RunLease, and ExecutorBoundary semantics, Dispatcher exactly-one Executor selection, sandbox and mutation authority, Runtime verification and EVIDENCE, Reviewer, Publisher, and no-retry and no-reroute boundaries remain unchanged by TASK-163 implementation.

Focused regression proves that after TASK-163 a compatible future default change can be expressed by editing only repository profile policy plus focused validation or smoke, with no required adapter, Dispatcher, Human carrier schema, durable dispatch schema, or lifecycle redesign. Adapter-mechanics regressions exercise explicitly injected profiles rather than duplicating the current repository default values as a second default authority.
